title: Joining sentences
description: Link ideas with and, or, but, so, because, if, when and that, and with the -e and -le forms of the verb.

guide.title: And, also, or, but
guide.text:
আর (aar) is the everyday 'and'; it also means 'more, else'. এবং (ebong) is the written, formal 'and'.

ও (o) is 'too, also, even'. It is attached to the END of the word it applies to: আমিও, 'I too'; এটাও, 'this one as well'. Between two nouns it can mean 'and': মা ও বাবা।

বা (baa) and অথবা (othobaa) are 'or' in statements. In a question offering a choice, 'or' is না (naa): চা না কফি? 'tea or coffee?'

কিন্তু (kintu) is 'but'. তবে (tobe) is a softer 'but, though, however'.

examples.english: I will have tea and biscuits.
I'd like to, but I have no time.

guide.title: So and because
guide.text:
তাই (taai) is 'so, therefore': বৃষ্টি হচ্ছে, তাই যাইনি - 'it's raining, so I haven't gone'.

কারণ (kaaron) is 'because' and comes, as in English, before the reason: আমি যাব না, কারণ আমার জ্বর।

The most natural spoken way puts the reason FIRST, followed by বলে (bole, literally 'having said'): আমার জ্বর বলে আমি যাব না - 'I have a fever, saying which, I won't go'.

জন্য (jonno) after a possessive also gives a reason: বৃষ্টির জন্য, 'because of the rain'; সেই জন্য or সেজন্য, 'for that reason'.

examples.english: It's raining, so I haven't gone.

examples.native: আমি যাব না, কারণ আমার জ্বর।
examples.roman: aami jaabo naa, kaaron aamaar jor.
examples.english: I won't go because I have a fever.

examples.native: আমার জ্বর বলে আমি যাব না।
examples.roman: aamaar jor bole aami jaabo naa.
examples.english: I won't go, as I have a fever.

guide.title: If and when: the -le form
guide.text:
The compact way to say 'if' or 'when' is a verb form ending in -লে (-le), made on the same stem as the simple past. It does not change for person.

করা - করলে (korle) if/when (someone) does
হওয়া - হলে (hole); যাওয়া - গেলে (gele); আসা - এলে (ele); খাওয়া - খেলে (khele); দেওয়া - দিলে (dile); পাওয়া - পেলে (pele)

বৃষ্টি হলে আমি যাব না - 'rain if-happens, I won't go'.
আপনি এলে আমরা খাব - 'you when-come, we will eat'.

The negative puts না BEFORE the verb: না হলে (naa hole) 'if not, otherwise'; আপনি না এলে, 'if you don't come'.

The fuller pattern uses the pair যদি (jodi) 'if' ... তাহলে (taahole) or তবে 'then', with ordinary tenses: যদি পারেন, তাহলে আসবেন।

তাহলে on its own is the conversational 'then, in that case'.

examples.english: If it rains, I won't go.
When you come, we will eat.

guide.title: Pairs: when ... then, what ... that
guide.text:
Bengali likes to build longer sentences in matched pairs: a word beginning with য- (j-) opens the first half, and its partner beginning with ত- or স- answers it in the second.

যখন (jokhon) when ... তখন (tokhon) then
যা (jaa) what ... তা (taa) or তাই (taai) that
যে (je) who, the one who ... সে (she) he/she
যেখানে (jekhaane) where ... সেখানে (shekhaane) there
যত (joto) as much ... তত (toto) so much

যখন সময় পাব, তখন করব - 'when I get time, then I'll do it'.
আপনি যা বলবেন, তাই হবে - 'what you say, just that will be'.

যে is also the plain 'that' after verbs of knowing and saying: আমি জানি যে সে আসবে, 'I know that he will come'. It is often left out.

examples.english: I'll do it when I get time.
It will be just as you say.
I know that he/she will come.

guide.title: Doing one thing after another
guide.text:
Two actions by the same person are joined not with 'and' but by putting the first verb in the -e form ('having done'): খেয়ে আসুন, 'having eaten, come'; বাড়ি গিয়ে ফোন করব, 'having gone home, I'll phone' - I'll phone when I get home.

'Before' and 'after' follow the verbal noun in the possessive: খাওয়ার পরে (khaaowaar pore) 'after eating'; যাওয়ার আগে (jaaowaar aage) 'before going'.

'While doing' is the -te form said twice: যেতে যেতে (jete jete) 'while going, on the way'; খেতে খেতে, 'while eating'.

examples.english: I'll phone when I get home.

ও is attached to the word it applies to.
